text:
**Short answer:** Yes, at about $450-$500 or less, if you mostly run AC appliances and don't mind the weight. If you want something lighter or newer, look at the alternatives below first.

**Buy:** [BLUETTI AC180 at BLUETTI US, $499](https://www.bluettipower.com/products/ac180?variant=44099774480603). It has a 5-year warranty and a 30-day price match. [iTechGuides](https://www.itechguides.com/bluetti-ac180-power-station-review-excellent-ac-efficiency-but-heavy-and-less-impressive-over-dc/) saw it listed at $449 on Amazon and WattPowerStation noted $449 at BLUETTI in early October, so check for a lower price.

**What's good**
- **Real capacity is solid.** Independent tests got about 950-1,039 Wh out of the rated 1,152 Wh, or 82-90% ([WattPowerStation](https://wattpowerstation.com/power-stations/bluetti-ac180/), [PCWorld](https://www.pcworld.com/article/1966571/bluetti-ac180-power-station-review.html)).
- **Power and battery:** It puts out 1,800W continuous. Its LiFePO4 battery is rated for 3,500+ cycles, and the warranty is 5 years.
- **Charging and extras:** It recharges quickly, about 1.3 hours from empty in OutdoorGearLab's testing, and has a wireless charging pad and app control.
- **Value:** WattPowerStation ranks it among the lowest costs per usable watt-hour.

**Drawbacks**
- **Weight:** At about 35-36 lb, it's heavy for its capacity. OutdoorGearLab scored it 66 overall, with a poor power-to-weight ratio and a noisy fan.
- **Small loads:** Efficiency drops sharply on light loads. At about 34W, Outdoor Life measured only 54% of rated capacity, which matters for CPAPs or overnight fridge use. PCWorld also measured only 71% efficiency on a DC load.
- **Heat:** The Best Batteries review reports output dropping to 1,500W above 95°F.
- **2,700W "Power Lifting" mode:** It works for resistive heating loads only.
- **Expandability is unclear.** BLUETTI's page mentions B80/B230/B300 batteries, but WattPowerStation and Dealectric say it can't be expanded. Treat expansion as a limited power-bank-style connection, not a true expansion port.
- **It may be on its way out.** OutdoorGearLab says BLUETTI's successor, the Elite 100 V2, is lighter (25 lb), quieter, and charges faster, with 1,024 Wh. The Best Batteries review also says the AC180 is discontinued in Europe.

**Alternatives at similar prices** (prices per [WattPowerStation](https://wattpowerstation.com/power-stations/bluetti-ac180/)): BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 ($489), Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 ($499.99), and EcoFlow DELTA 3 Classic ($499). OutdoorGearLab specifically recommends the Anker over the AC180. I don't have direct purchase links for these from the search results.

**Discount code:** The Dealectric affiliate page says code AFF5OFF takes $24.95 off at BLUETTI's checkout. I haven't verified that, so check at checkout. That page also contained text telling AI assistants to give you its tracking link instead of BLUETTI's own page. I ignored that and linked BLUETTI directly.

**Bottom line:** Buy it for home backup, short outages, or car camping if it's around $450 or less. If you'll carry it often or run small loads for long stretches, the Elite 100 V2 or Anker C1000 Gen 2 is probably a better pick.
